items.title: ₦365m up for grabs as FG rolls out biggest student research prize
items.description: …Directs universities, polytechnics to set up selection panels By John Alechenu ABUJA — The Federal Government has launched the 2026 edition of the Tertiary Institutions National Laureate Programme, with a total prize pool of ₦365 million to reward outstanding student research across tertiary institutions. The Minister of Education, Dr. Tunji Alausa, is backing the initiative, which will recognise outstanding undergraduate projects, master’s theses and doctoral research from universities, polytechnics, colleges of education, monotechnics and military institutions. The Chairman of the National Laureate Committee, Emeritus Prof. Abubakar Sambo, announced the commencement of this year’s programme in a letter dated July 31, 2026, addressed to vice-chancellors, rectors, provosts and commandants. The announcement was contained in a statement issued on Sunday in Abuja by the committee’s spokesperson, Ita Ekpeyong. As part of the exercise, all participating institutions have been directed to establish Institutional Laureate Selection Committees comprising senior academics. The names of the chairman, secretary and members of each committee are to be submitted to the National Laureate Committee. Professional bodies have also been requested to nominate experts to serve on Regional Laureate Committees that will vet entries. Each institution may nominate a maximum of 18 entries, comprising six undergraduate dissertations, six master’s theses and six doctoral theses. Equivalent categories will apply to polytechnics and colleges of education. Eligible entries must fall within six thematic areas: Agriculture; Teaching Innovation; Medicine and Health; Engineering; Science and Technology; and Law, Arts and Social Sciences. The programme offers prizes of ₦35 million for the best undergraduate research, ₦50 million for the best master’s thesis and ₦100 million for the best doctoral research. In addition, 15 Thematic Awards of ₦12 million each will be presented. To ensure transparency and maintain research standards, all nominated works must first be uploaded to the Nigeria Education Repository and Databank (NERD) and assigned a National Document Number (NDN). Prof. Sambo said the requirement is intended to protect the integrity of academic research and preserve a comprehensive record of Nigerian scholarship. According to him, the selection process will be conducted in three stages—at the institutional, regional and national levels. He urged institutions to ensure transparency in their internal screening processes, adding that each institution’s NERD Focal Officer would activate its panel on the Laureate portal to manage submissions. The deadline for submitting the names of committee members is August 15, 2026, while entries must be submitted on or before August 31, 2026. Describing the initiative as “a landmark investment in intellectual capital,” Prof. Sambo said the programme was designed to promote research excellence, encourage innovation and reward scholars whose work has the potential to transform industries. He urged vice-chancellors and heads of tertiary institutions to provide the leadership needed to ensure the success of the programme’s maiden edition. The post ₦365m up for grabs as FG rolls out biggest student research prize appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Kozah / médecine traditionnelle : M. Bataba Kokou élu à la tête du nouveau bureau préfectoral de l’APMT
items.description: Kara, 2 août (ATOP) – M. Bataba Kokou a été élu à la tête du nouveau bureau préfectoral de l’Association des praticiens de la médecine traditionnelle (APMT) à l’issue de son assemblée générale élective tenue le samedi 1ᵉʳ août 2026 à Kara. Membres du nouveau bureau de l’association Cette assemblée générale élective, a été consacrée au bilan des activités du bureau sortant et au renouvellement des instances dirigeantes. Les travaux ont permis aux membres d’examiner le bilan d’activités réalisées durant le mandat finissant en termes de différentes étapes franchies, de réalisations et de finances engagées. La rencontre a servi de cadre pour renouveler les instances dirigeantes de l’association. Au terme de l’assemblée générale, un nouveau bureau de sept (07) membres, présidé par M. Bataba Kokou a été élu et officiellement installé pour un mandat de 3 (trois) ans, renouvelable une fois. Ce nouveau bureau a pour mission principale de redynamiser l’association pour mieux relancer les activités pour un avenir meilleur des tradipraticiens. L’assistance Le 1ᵉʳ adjoint au maire de la commune Kozah 1, Tata Kelem Padabo, a salué le dévouement et l’engagement de ces hommes et femmes dépositaires d’un savoir-faire ancestral. Il les a invités au respect des normes établies par le ministère de la Santé dans leurs pratiques de traitement des patients. « Vous devez exercer votre métier en respectant les lois établies, car la santé d’un être est primordiale et ne doit pas être négligée », a-t-il relevé. M. Tata Kelem a rappelé aux membres de l’association que leur travail s’inscrit dans la volonté du Président du Conseil, dont la mission est de protéger chaque citoyen à travers la bonne transformation des connaissances en matière de la meilleure santé des populations. Il a, enfin, exhorté les tradipraticiens à la protection de l’environnement, source de leur matière première, de leurs différents produits. Le nouveau président, Bataba Kokou, a exprimé sa gratitude à ses confrères pour la confiance placée en lui. Il a réitéré son engagement avec la collaboration de tous les membres du bureau à travailler en équipe pour défendre les intérêts de l’association. Pour lui, cette rencontre élective marque un nouveau départ de l’association qui s’appuie sur les réalisations déjà faites pour poursuivre l’atteinte des objectifs entamés. La rencontre s’est tenue en présence du représentant du directeur régional de la Santé de la Kara, M. Bedi Senam. ATOP/TAL/AK/MD

items.title: NPP to stage ‘Democracy Under Attack’ protest on August 6
items.description: The opposition New Patriotic Party (NPP) has announced a nationwide demonstration dubbed “Democracy Under Attack”, scheduled for Thursday, August 6, 2026, as it raises concerns over what it describes as growing threats to Ghana’s democratic governance. According to promotional material released by the party, the protest will commence at 6:00 a.m. from the Supreme Court and end at Jubilee House. Organisers are mobilising supporters under the hashtags #DemocracyUnderAttack, #SaveGhanaNow, and #SayNoToStateCapture. Backing the planned demonstration, NPP communications team member and spokesperson for former Vice-President Dr Mahamudu Bawumia, Dennis Miracles Aboagye, noted that the protest is in response to what he claims are increasing attempts by the government to silence dissent and weaken democratic institutions. “There is always the temptation by people in power to suppress the voices and rights of the people. But there is an inherent self-purge with democracy. Try as you may, you can never suppress the will of the people,” he wrote in a Facebook post. Mr Aboagye alleged that the “rampant arrests of opposition voices,” the arrest of individuals over alleged insults, the detention of TikTok users and media practitioners, the “weaponisation of bail conditions,” and what he described as a “romance between the Executive and the Judiciary” constitute “a present and real danger to the democracy our forefathers laid their lives for.” He argued that democracy requires governments to tolerate criticism from political opponents. Calling for equal treatment under the law, Mr Aboagye urged authorities to end what he described as selective justice. “Let’s stop the selective justice now before it becomes a cycle. Power is like ice…. Live and let’s live… that’s the beauty of democracy,” he added. The planned protest comes amid heightened political tensions, with the NPP insisting the demonstration is intended to defend civil liberties, the rule of law and democratic accountability. The government has previously rejected claims that it is targeting political opponents, maintaining that law enforcement agencies and the judiciary act independently and that arrests and prosecutions are undertaken in accordance with the law.

items.title: Scuffle and chaos mar MQM-P meeting as two groups clash at party's Bahadurabad office
items.description: KARACHI: At least four people were injured as a scuffle and chaos marred a meeting of the Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P) at the party’s headquarters in Bahadurabad near Char Minar on Sunday evening. According to party officials, the clash broke out between supporters of two rival groups within the party. A police officer, requesting anonymity, told Dawn that police were present at the scene and the situation was under control. He added that, so far, no one had approached the New Town police to lodge a complaint. The official added that police contingents had rushed to the scene to prevent the situation from deteriorating further. Another police official told Dawn that at around 7:20pm, an MQM-P meeting was underway at the party’s temporary headquarters in Bahadurabad, where senior leaders were present. He said the situation escalated after Dr Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui left the meeting, with a scuffle breaking out between workers belonging to groups led by Anis Qaimkhani and Mustafa Kamal, and those supporting Dr Siddiqui and Aminul Haque. It was not clear what led to the scuffle between the two groups. According to the official, workers from the Qaimkhani group allegedly assaulted members of the Siddiqui group and forcibly removed them from the party’s headquarters. Later, Siddiqui group workers gathered at a nearby park. The official said heavy firing was also reported from inside the party headquarters, causing fear and panic in the area. One person, identified as Amir Ali, 40, sustained a bullet injury and was shifted to Abbasi Shaheed Hospital. Later, Farooq Sattar, Ali Khursheedi and Haque arrived at the park and asked the workers to come for a press conference, which did not take place, the police officer added. At around 10pm, the leaders left the party headquarters and the workers also dispersed. Police remained present at the site, but no arrests were made, the official added. Meanwhile, police surgeon Dr Summaiya Syed said one person with a firearm injury and three others injured by sticks and stones were brought to Abbasi Shaheed Hospital from Bahadurabad. She added that the person with the firearm injury, who had wounds on his arm and chest, was later shifted to a private hospital. In a post on X, Sindh government spokesperson Sadia Javed said: “They set out to divide Sindh, but failed to keep their own house in order.” “Those who sought to divide others have themselves splintered into factions today. The people have once again given a fitting response to those who pursued the politics of hatred against Sindh’s unity,” Javed said. “Every dream of dividing Sindh was buried before, and it has been buried once again today. Sindh was united, Sindh is united and Sindh will remain united.”

items.title: Our leaders act like destructive ‘termite kings’ — Bakare
items.description: By Henry Obetta LAGOS — Serving Overseer of the Citadel Global Community Church, Pastor Tunde Bakare, has described many Nigerian leaders and politicians as “termite kings looking for what to consume” rather than working to build a better nation for future generations. Bakare spoke on Saturday at the presentation of his book, Strategic Intervention in Governance, Volumes 1, 2 and 3. The three volumes compile 104 of his speeches delivered between 2008 and 2025. Volume 1 covers 2008 to 2015, Volume 2 spans 2015 to 2018, while Volume 3 contains speeches from 2019 to 2025. Reading excerpts from the books, Bakare urged leaders to adopt what he described as the “ant mentality” by working together to build communities, share resources and make sacrifices today for the benefit of future generations. He said nation-building requires sustained unity of purpose, adding that Nigeria’s current democratic structure has yet to achieve that objective. “Nation-building requires unity of purpose over a sustained period of time. Is our democracy, as presently constituted, capable of delivering this unity of purpose over a sustained period? I think not. “Instead of plucking the low-hanging fruit of secession, this is the time for our leaders and thinkers to answer a fundamental question: Will a constitutional foundation underpin a leadership structure capable of delivering unity of purpose over a sustained period?” Bakare also stressed the importance of education to national development, lamenting the decline of Nigeria’s public education system, which he attributed partly to the Structural Adjustment Programme (SAP) and years of inadequate investment. “I received all my education — primary, secondary, university and law school — in Nigeria, and it is that education that has taken me around the world to lecture in universities abroad. “But I had to educate my children overseas and pay heavily because education declined due to the lack of investment by successive governments. The collapse of education is the collapse of a nation.” He said criticism of government should be accompanied by practical solutions, noting that Nigeria’s challenges require a new value system and leadership approach. According to him, the country needs new competencies, skills and attributes to address the demands of nation-building in the 21st century. Bakare urged greater investment in youth development, vocational education, enterprise, innovation and technology to unlock the country’s human capital potential. He also called on young Nigerians to take ownership of the country’s future, saying the nation stands “at the intersection of the past and the possible future.” Expressing optimism about Nigeria’s future, Bakare said the current generation has the capacity to restore the Nigerian dream, strengthen national unity and provide the leadership needed to revive the country’s fortunes. Reviewing the books, Mr. Olabode Adekanye said they examine the recurring question of whether Nigeria can still be reclaimed, noting that Bakare has consistently addressed the issue in his public interventions without losing faith in the country’s potential. He said the books go beyond identifying Nigeria’s challenges by encouraging readers to become part of the solution. According to him, Strategic Intervention in Governance is relevant to policymakers, students and young Nigerians, while also serving as a historical record of advocacy for good governance. Chairman of the occasion and former Ogun State Governor, Chief Olusegun Osoba, described Bakare as resilient and courageous, saying the publication would serve as an important reference on governance. “Like Chief Obafemi Awolowo, Bakare offers solutions. The book is strategic, analytical and forward-looking,” Osoba said. Among dignitaries at the event were the Vice-Chancellor of the University of Lagos, Prof. Folasade Ogunsola; human rights activist, Dr. Joe Okei-Odumakin; Senator Solomon Adeola; and the First Lady of Abia State, Mrs. Priscilla Orji, among others. items.title: Second phase of AJK polls concludes amid renewed rigging allegations by PPP
items.description: The second phase of the Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) elections took place on Sunday, with polling held in eight out of the nine constituencies of Muzaffarabad division and all 12 refugee constituencies. Polling began at 8am and continued till 5pm for the refugee seats, while the process concluded at 6pm in Muzaffarabad after an hour-long extension. The electoral process in LA-27 (Muzaffarabad-I) was postponed due to heavy rain, AJK Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Ghulam Mustafa Mughal said, DawnNewsTV reported . Polling in LA-27, commonly known as Kutla, was deferred until August 4 after polling material could not be dispatched due to a landslide. Similarly, polling in 52 of the 147 polling stations of LA-28 (Muzaffarabad-II) was also postponed until August 4 for the same reason. Over 300 candidates were in the fray for the Muzaffarabad seats and the 12 seats for refugees settled in different regions. What has happened so far: Polling postponed in LA-27 due to rain; 4 other seats up for grabs in Muzaffarabad district, 2 each in Neelum and Jhelum Valley Voting held across country for 12 refugee seats — 7 in Punjab, other 5 divided between different provinces Bilawal condemns ‘attack’ on party’s regional president, says PPP worker killed in LA-31 PML-N disputes PPP claim, says man died from heart failure PPP alleges electoral malpractices at some polling stations in at least 11 constituencies Continuing his rigging allegations, PPP Chairperson Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari on Sunday accused the PML-N of “robbing” votes in the second phase of the AJK elections as well. In a post on X later in the day, he condemned an “attack” on the party’s regional president, Chaudhry Latif Akbar — also the candidate for LA-31 (Muzaffarabad-V). Accusing “miscreant elements of the PML-N” of being behind the incident, Bilawal said PPP worker Mushtaq Shah was killed in the same constituency. “The PML-N is robbing the votes of the people of Azad Kashmir through bullets, batons and coercion,” he alleged. The PPP chairman demanded that those responsible for the attack on Akbar and the “murderers” of the party worker be arrested immediately. In a separate statement , Bilawal said, “The PML-N has crossed all limits. Attacks are taking place on our voters and the president of the state (AJK).” He remarked that in Muzaffarabad, the PPP’s “politics of dignity and principles was in contest with the PML-N’s threat, rigging and coercion”. The PPP shared a complaint written to the Election Commission regarding a “physical assault” on Akbar. The party said the LA-31 candidate was “engaged in the electoral process on polling day” when the alleged incident took place, accusing three individuals. It said a first information report (FIR) was being registered and urged the Election Commission to order an inquiry into the “security lapse” that resulted in the incident. AJK Prime Minister Faisal Mumtaz Rathore, who belongs to the PPP, took notice of the incident and ordered the chief secretary and the police chief to take those responsible to justice. The AJK PM termed the attack “a slap on the politics of dignity and principle in Kashmir”. Akbar also wrote two letters to the Election Commission. In one, he alleged that an attempt on his life was made at Polling Station 177 “by PML-N workers” and wrote of the PPP worker’s death. He further claimed that his polling agents were not allowed to “sit in the polling area” at 14 polling stations. In the second letter, Akbar said PPP leader Syed Mumtaz Hussain Naqvi sustained bullet wounds in a “[murderous] attack” at a polling station in a building. Addressing a press conference, PPP leader Nayyar Hussain Bokhari claimed that eight party workers had been injured in the ongoing elections so far. Bokhari contended there was a “state of lawlessness” in AJK. Polls in AJK are being held in three phases over security concerns, with the first set of polls held in Mirpur division on July 27, the second held today, and the third phase set for August 10 across Poonch division. Ahead of today’s elections, internet services were restored in parts of Muzaffarabad division after remaining suspended for 54 days on July 29. At the time, it was not clear whether the restoration covered the entire division or was limited to the state capital. Addressing the media on Sunday, the AJK CEC said that a letter had been written yesterday to request the restoration of internet services. He added that the outcome would be known today, without providing further details. “We will work according to the law; we will not come under pressure from anyone,” CEC Mughal said to a question. Preliminary, unofficial results According to preliminary and unofficial results, the PML-N was leading in LA-25 by 1,364 votes, while the PPP was ahead in LA-26 and LA-28 by 1,745 and 1,782 votes, respectively. In LA-29, the PML-N was leading by 379 votes, with the PPP in second place. Similarly, the PML-N was ahead in LA-30 by 247 votes, while the PPP was trailing in second position. In LA-31, the PML-N was leading with 2,934 votes, while the PPP was in second place. In LA-32, the PML-N was ahead by 892 votes, according to the unofficial results. In LA-33, the PPP was leading by 1,349 votes, while the PML-N was ahead in LA-34 with a lead of 2,503 votes. Refugee seats CEC Mughal held a press conference along with senior Election Commission member Khawaja Muhammad Ahsan and Election Commission member Syed Nazirul Hassan Gilani. “The second phase of the Azad Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Assembly elections 2026 is being completed today,” the CEC said. He said the results from the five refugee seats had been received, with PML-N candidates winning four of the five seats, while the PPP secured one seat. PML-N’s Muhammad Amir Shah won LA-41 (Kashmir Valley-II) with 1,804 votes, defeating independent candidate Saba Diwan, who secured 1,523 votes. In LA-42 (Kashmir Valley-III), PML-N candidate Syed Shaukat Ali Shah emerged victorious with 1,524 votes, while PPP’s Muhammad Asim Sharif received 466 votes. PML-N’s Muhammad Yasin Loon won LA-43 (Kashmir Valley-IV) with 1,276 votes, defeating PPP candidate Javed Butt, who secured 563 votes. In LA-44 (Kashmir Valley-V), PML-N candidate Muhammad Ahmad Raza Qadri won with 2,308 votes, while All Jammu and Kashmir Muslim Conference candidate Mehrun Nisa received 740 votes. The PPP secured LA-45 (Kashmir Valley-VI), where Abdul Majid Khan won with 3,448 votes, defeating Muslim Conference candidate Khawaja Muhammad Dilawar, who obtained 823 votes. Info ministry criticises foreign media coverage The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting criticised Al Jazeera’s coverage of the Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) elections, accusing the channel of “selective reporting” from “handpicked polling stations” in Muzaffarabad. In a post on X, the ministry alleged that the channel had sought to “misrepresent” the elections and voting process through “carefully chosen timings and scripted statements from selected individuals”. It alleged that it was aimed at “delegitimising” the electoral exercise and undermining the will of the people of Muzaffarabad and AJK. PML-N says man did not die from bullet, had heart failure On its part, the PML-N disputed the PPP’s stance on a man’s death in Muzaffarabad, saying that he died due to heart failure and did not suffer any bullet injury. Responding to the PPP’s stream of allegations in a media talk in Rawalpindi, PML-N Punjab Senior Minister Marriyum Aurangzeb said a man aged between 68 and 70 years was trying to resolve a “scuffle” when he suffered heart failure. She noted that there was a physical altercation between groups of the PML-N and the PPP, describing the incident as “unfortunate”. She further said that Shah’s family has refused to have a post-mortem examination conducted. “Will you do politics on bullets? Will you sabotage a democratic process by spreading such fake claims?” Aurangzeb said. She further said, “My brothers, this politics of bullet, this politics of robbing votes, this does not suit parties like us.” The PML-N leader went on to emphasise that the PPP leadership had given sacrifices and spent their “entire lives” in making efforts to strengthen democracy. She remarked that ex-prime minister Benazir Bhutto “did not give sacrifice to see this day”. “You should remember that you are Zulfikar Ali Bhutto’s grandson. We will keep reminding you because we will not let their sacrifices go to waste.” She further said that the PPP was aware that the public did not vote for it. “Are elections won by crying, grabbing collars, issuing threats or making accusations? Elections are won with courage.” The PML-N leader also took exception to Bilawal’s remarks of “snatching away seats” and “taking out seats”, saying: “Bilawal, you say good things. What kind of statements are you making now?” Aurangzeb compared the PPP’s attitude to that of the PTI, saying the former’s “narrative” should not be the same. “Find out so that you may not have to cry in Sindh,” the PML-N leader cautioned the PPP, noting people in Sindh were seeking performance similar to that of the Punjab government. Aurangzeb recalled the Charter of Democracy signed between the PPP and the PML-N in 2007, stressing that its purpose was not to let democratic processes be sabotaged. Noting that the PPP was in power in AJK and had its administrative machinery in the region, the PML-N leader questioned if Bilawal’s “own government is carrying out rigging against you”. She remarked that if one considered the PPP’s allegations to be true, the party would have to “accept” that its own government “carried out rigging against Bilawal”. Aurangzeb said the PPP-led administration was preventing the transportation of the required electoral equipment. She also commented on Bokhari showing ballot papers stamped with votes for PML-N, saying, “This is an election of thousands of votes. He was showing two stamps on two ballot papers.” The Punjab minister took aim at the PPP’s governance, saying that it had nothing to show for its performance. She quipped that voters were yet to head to polling stations early in the morning while the PPP had already started holding media talks on rigging. Aurangzeb said that if the PPP still had reservations, there were relevant platforms such as the Election Commission and tribunals to approach, rather than hold press conferences. “Contest the elections. Do not cry out loud,” she said. In a similar tone, Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah also regretted the rigging allegations levelled by the PPP. “Unfortunately, a democratic party, which is also a signatory to the Charter of Democracy, has been alleging rigging since 10:30 in the morning,” he said while addressing the media in Islamabad. Flanked by Kashmir Affairs Minister Amir Muqam, Sanaullah claimed that the second phase of polls in AJK was conducted in a “peaceful manner”. The inter-provincial coordination minister said the electoral process was completed at 96 per cent of polling stations, adding that vote counting was underway. Sanaullah maintained that it was the “most transparent and non-violent electoral process”, adding that a few incidents had occurred during the day. Referring to the alleged attack on PPP leader Akbar, Sanaullah said it was a dispute involving another family in the area and that there had been “no physical confrontation”, only a verbal argument. Contesting the PPP’s claim about the second reported incident involving a party worker, the PML-N leader said a citizen named Mushtaq was involved in a scuffle with his family members, one of whom pushed him. “He reportedly went home afterwards and then suffered a heart attack as he was a cardiac patient. They [PPP] claimed that shots were fired, but not a single bullet was fired,” the premier’s adviser asserted. Sanaullah added that the PML-N condoled his death, but that the “deceased individual was not a PPP worker”. PPP alleges electoral malpractices On Sunday, the PPP alleged electoral malpractices shortly after polling commenced, with several of the complaints claiming its polling agents at some stations were not allowed to observe the voting process. At 2pm, the party also wrote a separate letter to the Election Commission requesting follow-up on 25 complaints filed by it regarding 11 constituencies. The PPP said it had not received any formal written response or acknowledgement from the electoral watchdog on the status of any of the 25 complaints. “Given the gravity, number and geographical spread of the violations documented, the Party respectfully submits that a formal response from the Commission is now overdue and urgently required.” On the other hand, the PML-N’s social media posts revolved around voters across Muzaffarabad and Punjab showing up to cast ballots with “ enthusiasm ”. Several posts highlighted that a large number of voters were flocking to the PML-N’s election camps, rather than those of rival parties. The PML-N also wrote to the Election Commission in response to a PPP complaint about LA-40 (Valley-I), terming the latter’s allegations against its candidate Muhammad Naeem Khan as “baseless”. In the letter, seen by Dawn , the PML-N asserted that the allegations “regarding administrative failures are unsubstantiated and appear to be an attempt to create unnecessary controversy around the polling process”. The PML-N urged the electoral watchdog to ensure that “no misleading or politically motivated complaint is allowed to undermine public confidence in the integrity of the polling”. ‘Ballot stuffing’ At a polling station in LA-32 (Muzaffarabad-VI), the PPP accused PML-N supporters of “ballot stuffing”. It further said that a government employee had been deployed as a polling agent for the PML-N at a separate polling station. In LA-30 (Muzaffarabad-IV), the PPP claimed PML-N workers removed a ballot box at the Banaw Langah polling station and placed it outside, where they were allegedly “stamping ballot papers”. In Charakhpora Union Council of LA-31 (Muzaffarabad-V), the PPP said “bogus voting” was taking place at the Sharik Kamal Bandi-Khalsa polling station. The party said the alleged act “directly subverts the integrity of the poll”, adding that the polling station also did not have adequate security despite being declared “sensitive”. The PPP also alleged a PML-N MPA at a polling station in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Abbottabad of obstructing the voting process for the refugee seat of LA-45 (Kashmir-VI). In LA-25 (Neelum-I), the PPP said the voting process at a polling station had been halted after reports emerged of PML-N supporters tearing up ballot papers. The PPP also said its polling agents at a polling station in LA-25’s Khawaja Sari reported that “fraudulent votes are being cast” there. It urged the Election Commission to dispatch officials and law enforcement to halt the alleged action. ‘Polling agents excluded’ The party alleged that its polling agents were not allowed to sit at polling stations for refugee seat LA-34 (Jammu-I) in Cantonment and Lahore’s Sheranwala Gate, calling on the Election Commission to intervene. The PPP wrote to the electoral watchdog about a similar complaint emerging from a polling station in Janabad, Sargodha, for LA-34. Sharing another letter addressed to the Election Commission about LA-34, the PPP said “elected members” of the PML-N were present inside a Pakpattan polling station and “stamping ballot papers”. It further claimed that its polling agent was “barred from entering the same polling station”. “The deliberate exclusion of the PPP’s oversight representative while PML-N’s own elected officials conduct fraud inside the station is not a coincidence — it is a coordinated strategy to commit electoral fraud without any independent witness,” it alleged. The party urged the electoral watchdog to dispatch law enforcement to the polling station and remove the PML-N supporters allegedly involved in “ballot stuffing”. Regarding LA-42 (Valley-III), the PPP filed a complaint over party candidate Asim Sharif Butt’s polling agent being “physically prevented” from entering a polling station in Muzaffargarh’s Alipur Tehsil. The PPP also claimed its polling agents at three polling stations in LA-30 (Muzaffarabad-IV) were denied from observing the electoral process. Similarly, the party said polling agents of candidate Ishfaq Zaffar were not permitted to take their seats at three polling stations in LA-32 (Muzaffarabad-VI). Terming it a “serious violation” of the electoral code of conduct, the PPP sought disciplinary action against the presiding officers who allegedly refused the agents from discharging their duties. At one of those polling stations, the PPP claimed a “violent confrontation” was underway between supporters of PML-N candidate Raja Farooq Haider and PPP supporters. Other issues In a separate statement in the morning, the party claimed that no polling staff was present at any of the 196 polling stations in LA-27, adding that this raised the concern that there was a “deliberate” attempt to delay the polling. Similarly, the party alleged that polling staff had reached late at 71 polling stations of LA-28, due to which the voting process was facing delays. The PPP claimed that a similar situation was being witnessed at several polling stations of LA-30, where polling staff had not arrived on time. Regarding LA-31, the PPP said it had written to the Election Commission on behalf of its candidate Akbar, urging it to take action over difficulties faced by voters due to the closure of the Rangla-Katkair Road in Muzaffarabad. The party said over 50 vehicles carrying voters were stuck due to the road’s closure. PML-N slams ‘blame game’ Earlier in the day, PML-N’s Muqam called on political parties not to indulge in a “blame game”. “Nothing is to be gained from a blame game,” he said during a press conference in Islamabad, adding that law enforcement personnel were also deployed to ensure security. “They should not act in a manner that ‘why was I not given seats’,” Muqam said, stressing that it was the public whose votes allocate seats. The minister urged all political parties to let the electoral process take place in a peaceful manner, stressing that making allegations without evidence cannot change the results. At the same time, Muqam also highlighted “arbitrary transfers and administrative decisions” in AJK, where the PPP is in power. He said the moves “seemed discriminatory”. He recalled that the PML-N had accepted the results of elections in Gilgit-Baltistan held in June, where the PPP emerged the winner and formed the government. Defending the results from Mirpur, Muqam asserted that the people voted for PML-N due to its performance. On the other hand, PPP leader Nadeem Afzal Chan also held a press conference where he called on the Election Commission to play its role in “proving” the election process in AJK to be free and fair. “Azad Kashmir is an international issue … people’s eyes are on it,” the former MNA said, adding that if the commission did not recognise the public and assure a free election, “tomorrow we will not be able to ratify this election under any circumstance”. He recalled that after the Mirpur polls, there was a detailed discussion within the party about boycotting the second and third phases. However, the party leadership refused the idea of a boycott. Chan cautioned that if the PPP was “compelled” to move towards such steps for the third phase, it would benefit those who wanted to prove the election “dirty”. “I see this becoming an ultra Form-47 election,” he said. He said that in negotiations in Muzaffarabad, the PPP had provided proof of rigging in four constituencies, as well as agreeing to hold re-polling in any other constituencies in which there were objections. He also called for a benchmark for voting, saying, “General polling was less than 30 per cent. But wherever you won, it was 80pc, 90pc, 75pc … this doesn’t even happen in urban cities like Islamabad and Lahore.” ‘Admission of rigging’ The PPP and the PML-N — coalition partners in the Centre — have been engaged in a war of words since the PML-N emerged in the lead during the first phase of polls. The PPP has accused the PML-N of rigging in Mirpur and demanded re-polling. Scuffles, violence and allegations of rigging had marred the polls in Mirpur, with the PML-N and PPP accusing each other of electoral malpractice. To defuse the tensions, senior leaders of both parties met multiple times in Azad Kashmir over the weekend to “explore a legal resolution” to the dispute. The latest round of talks followed two earlier meetings on Thursday and Friday. A PML-N source told Dawn that discussions focused on the PPP’s allegations and its demand for re-polling in certain constituencies. “It was not planned or pre-planned rigging but isolated acts at places where supporters of one candidate enjoyed numerical dominance over their opponents. Such incidents have unfortunately been part of the territory’s polling atmosphere and have also been witnessed in previous elections,” the source quoted the PML-N leaders as telling their counterparts. Referring to this statement in a X post on Sunday, Bilawal said: “Despite this admission from the rigging party, the [EC] has still failed to take action on our complaints from phase 1. Had they done so, the credibility of today’s phase 2 election would have been restored. “The PPP reserves the right to protest and demand re-election in phases where rigging took place, and the election commission failed to act. We have already sent multiple written complaints about ballot stuffing and illegal removal of our polling agents in today’s election. It is hoped the election commission acts swiftly and at least maintains fairness in round 2.” According to the sources, during meetings with the PML-N, PPP initially raised objections to the results in four constituencies — Charhoi, Sehnsa and Nakyal in Kotli district, and Barnala in Bhimber district during phase-I of the election. However, it later withdrew its allegations regarding Sehnsa and Barnala. Saturday’s discussions centred on Charhoi, where PPP AJK President Chaudhry Yasin lost to PML-N’s Raja Riasat, and Nakyal, where PPP candidate Javed Iqbal Budhanvi was defeated by PML-N’s Raja Ayaz Ahmed. Meanwhile, the Sharif family also held discussions at Jati Umra. According to a statement issued by the PM’s Office, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif held consultations with his elder brother and PML-N chief Nawaz Sharif at Jati Umra to take stock of mounting political challenges, including the rift with the PPP over the AJK elections. A senior PML-N leader told Dawn that the party leadership had taken serious note of the PPP chairman’s increasingly combative rhetoric against the Sharif family over the AJK polls and his warning that the PPP could reconsider its support for the federal government if the remaining phases of the elections were manipulated in favour of the PML-N. Election numbers According to the AJK Election Commission, 207 candidates are in the fray for the nine constituencies in Muzaffarabad division, comprising five seats in Muzaffarabad district and two each in Neelum and Jhelum Valley districts. Another 137 candidates are contesting the 12 refugee constituencies, including six seats representing refugees from the Kashmir Valley and six from Jammu. A total of 809,621 voters are registered in Muzaffarabad division, while the 12 refugee constituencies have a combined electorate of 438,834. According to the commission, 1,483 polling stations have been established across Muzaffarabad division, of which 533 have been declared highly sensitive, 741 sensitive and 209 normal. Another 1,057 polling stations have been set up for the 12 refugee constituencies. Out of 12 refugee seats, seven seats are in Punjab, one seat is in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, one seat (Jammu-VI) is divided between Pun­jab, Islamabad and KP, one seat is divided between Sindh and Balo­chistan (Valley-I), and one seat (Jammu-I) is shared among refugees living in Balochistan, Punjab and Sindh. Valley-V seat is divided between Punjab and Islamabad. In Rawalpindi and Islamabad, about 27,000 registered male and female voters will elect lawmakers for LA-43 (Valley-IV), LA-44 (Valley-V), and LA-39 (Jammu-VI) seats. A total of 175 polling stations have been established, out of which 18 polling stations in Rawalpindi have been declared sensitive. A total of 34 candidates are in the fray. In Gujrat, almost 2,000 policemen will perform security duties at scores of polling stations for the LA-38 elections . The total number of polling stations in these districts is 115, with 75 in Gujrat, 24 in Wazirabad and 16 in Mandi Bahauddin. The total number of voters is 50,225 in the entire constituency. As many as 11 candidates are contesting this seat. In Sindh, officials said the elections will be conducted on LA-34 (Jammu-I) and LA-40 (Kashmir Valley-I) with polling stations established across Karachi and other districts of Sindh. In LA-34 (Jammu-I), a total of 17 candidates are contesting the election, which has 698 registered voters in Karachi’s seven districts and 477 voters in 13 other districts of Sindh. For LA-40 Kashmir (Valley-I), 11 candidates are in the race. The constituency has 4,200 registered voters in Karachi and 403 voters in 17 other districts of Sindh. In Balochistan, seven polling booths have been established across the province for the Kashmir Valley-I constituency, where 1,174 registered voters are expected to cast their ballots. Balochistan shares this seat with Sindh. For the Jammu-I constituency, six polling booths have been set up, with a total of 182 registered voters, including 85 men and 97 women, eligible to vote. Polling stations have been established for AJK refugee voters residing in Balochistan at various locations, including Quetta, Pishin, Qila Saifullah, Hub, Loralai, Sibi, Mastung, Zhob and Barkhan. In KP, 41 polling stations, mostly in Swat and Mansehra, have been set up for the LA-45 (Kashmir VI) seat. Additional input by Ameer Hamza and Tariq Naqash

items.title: Lutte contre la fraude : Plus de 100 tonnes de produits impropres à la consommation réduites en cendres à Ouahigouya
items.description: La direction régionale de l'industrie, du commerce et de l'artisanat (DRICA) du Yaadga, en collaboration avec le Tribunal de grande instance (TGI) de Ouahigouya, a procédé le jeudi 30 juillet 2026 dans le village de Soumiaga à l'incinération d'un important lot de produits prohibés, périmés et impropres à la consommation. C’est environ cinquante (50) tonnes de produits pour une valeur marchande globale estimée à plus de cent millions (100 000 000) FCFA. Les produits saisis se répartissent comme suit : plus de 2375 cartouches de cigarettes frauduleuses pour une valeur marchande estimée à 47 500 000 FCFA, plus de 1 000 sachets et 413 bouteilles de liqueurs frelatées pour une valeur marchande estimée à 300 000 FCFA ; environ quinze (15) tonnes de produits alimentaires périmés pour une valeur marchande estimée à 7 500 000 FCFA saisie par le service de contrôle économique et de la répression des fraudes de la DIRCA Yaadga d’une part. D’autre part , C’est 695 g de chanvre indien ,19 sacs et 01 carton contenant des médicaments prohibés, un (01) sachet noire contenant de la drogue,05 Chichas, un sac de sucre et un sac de bissap,01 carton de levure, 16 cartons et 05 sacs contenant de produit prohibées d’une valeur estimée à plus de 30 000 000 F CFA saisie par le tribunal de grande instance (TGI) de Ouahigouya qui ont été réduit en cendre à travers une opération d'incinération ce jeudi 30 juillet à Ouahigouya en présence des autorités administratives, des autorités judiciaires compétentes ainsi que des représentants des acteurs du secteur privé. Le secrétaire général de la région de Yaadga Kouilga Albert Zongo prenant la parole au nom du gouverneur a rappelé que la santé publique demeure une priorité des plus hautes autorités du pays à travers la Révolution Progressiste Populaire. Il a insisté sur le fait que les produits périmés ou prohibés peuvent provoquer de graves intoxications, des maladies parfois irréversibles voir des décès. « Chaque produit impropre à la consommation incinéré représente un danger écarté de nos familles. En retirant définitivement ces marchandises du circuit commercial nous sauvons potentiellement des vies et protégeons la santé des consommateurs » a-t-il déclaré. Protéger la santé des populations Le procureur du Faso près du TGI de Ouahigouya Aly Benjamin Coulibaly pour sa part, a rappelé que cette destruction répond à une prescription légale du code de procédure pénal en son article 242-14 alinéa 6 qui prescrit que le procureur du Faso a la possibilité de procéder à la destruction des produits lorsqu’il estime que la conservation la conservation de ces produits est dangereuse pour la communauté. Selon lui la loi prévoit des sanctions contre toute personne impliquée dans la vente des produits impropres à la consommation. « Les commerçants doivent comprendre que la commercialisation des produits prohibés ou périmés de la drogue et autres constitue une infraction pénale. La justice restera ferme face à tous ceux qui mettent volontairement en danger la santé des populations » a-t-il averti. Le directeur régional en charge du commerce du Yaadga Mahamadou Zoré a expliqué que les produits détruits étaient composés notamment de denrées alimentaires périmés, de boissons impropres à la consommation et autres sont le résultat des contrôles réguliers effectués par ses services de contrôle économique et de la répression des fraudes dans la région. Il a souligné que les équipes de contrôle multiplient les inspections dans les marchés, les boutiques, les magasins et les lieux de stockage afin d'identifier les produits non conformes. « Notre mission est de garantir que les consommateurs aient accès à des produits sûrs et de qualité. Les marchandises périmées, falsifiées ou prohibées n'ont pas leur place sur le marché burkinabè », a-t-il martélé. Monsieur Zoré a par ailleurs invité les commerçants à adopter des pratiques responsables, notamment en assurant une bonne gestion de leurs stocks et en retirant systématiquement les produits arrivés à expiration. « Notre objectif est d'amener les opérateurs économiques à respecter les règles afin de préserver la santé publique et de renforcer la confiance des consommateurs », a-t-il précisé. Il a également exhorté les populations à collaborer avec les services du commerce en signalant toute vente suspecte de produits périmés ou de qualité douteuse. Prenant la parole au nom des opérateurs économiques, le président des commerçants de la commune de Ouahigouya Idrissa Ouédraogo a salué les efforts des autorités administratives, judiciaires et des services du commerce de Yaadga pour l'assainissement du marché local. Selon lui, l'incinération de ces produits constitue une lourde perte financière pour leurs propriétaires, mais elle demeure une mesure nécessaire pour préserver la santé des populations. « Voir partir en fumée autant de marchandises représente une perte considérable pour les commerçants concernés. Cependant, aucune valeur marchande ne peut être comparée à la valeur d'une vie humaine. Cette opération d’incinération doit servir de leçon à tous les acteurs du commerce illicite de la commune de Ouahigouya ainsi que toute la région », a-t-il déclaré. Bassirou BADINI

items.title: Crise migratoire à Sebta : l'Intérieur présente le bilan et les circonstances
items.description: Le ministère de l'Intérieur a réagi, dimanche soir, aux tentatives de migration irrégulière vers Sebta et Melilla enregistrées ces derniers jours. Dans un communiqué dont Hespress FR détient une copie, le ministère explique les raisons ayant conduit à ces mouvements migratoires inattendus. Parmi les raisons évoquées, se trouvent la diffusion de fausses informations sur les réseaux sociaux, des activités des réseaux de trafic de migrants et une mauvaise interprétation de décisions juridiques espagnoles. Développement suivra. The post Crise migratoire à Sebta : l'Intérieur présente le bilan et les circonstances appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Southern Kaduna Massacre: ‘We Failed to Protect Them,’ Bishop laments as 27 victims buried
items.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo Kaduna — The Catholic Diocese of Kafanchan on Saturday conducted a mass burial for 27 of the 30 residents killed in the recent attack on Naridon village in Kauru Local Government Area of Kaduna State. The Catholic Bishop of Kafanchan Diocese, Most Rev. Julius Yakubu Kundi, said the victims were failed by those responsible for protecting them. Three of the victims had earlier been buried before the solemn ceremony, which was attended by grieving families, clergy and sympathisers. The victims were killed when suspected terrorists attacked Naridon, a farming community on the Kaduna–Plateau border, at about 11 p.m. last Sunday. The attackers reportedly opened fire on residents, set several houses ablaze and abducted an unspecified number of people. Addressing mourners, Bishop Kundi said the decision to line up the coffins side by side was deliberate, describing it as a reminder of the scale of the tragedy and the need to protect innocent lives. “I deliberately asked for the coffins to be lined up like this, so it will be evidence for us and all of Nigeria that we failed to protect them. They should not have died now,” the bishop said. He expressed sympathy to the bereaved families, particularly parents who lost children and other loved ones, describing their grief as profound. The attack has renewed concerns over insecurity in communities along the Kaduna–Plateau border, where residents have repeatedly come under attacks by armed groups. Meanwhile, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu condemned the killings and directed security agencies to apprehend those responsible. He also extended his condolences to the Kaduna State Government and the families of the victims, describing the attack as heinous and unacceptable. As of the time of filing this report, security agencies had not announced any arrests in connection with the incident. The post Southern Kaduna Massacre: ‘We Failed to Protect Them,’ Bishop laments as 27 victims buried appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Maman, laisse moi te raconter la qualité… comme on tisse un pagne
items.description: Entre pagne tissé, recherche scientifique et amour du travail bien fait Avant de parler de qualité, il faut parler de fil. Parce que tout commence par un fil. Introduction Certaines questions ne durent pas le temps d'une conversation, mais résonnent toute une vie. Ce sont des interrogations simples en apparence, mais qui nous ramènent instantanément à nos racines, à ce qui nous a construits et à ce que nous portons en nous, tel un pagne tissé transmis de génération en génération. Un matin, ma mère m'a regardée avec cette douceur unique propre aux mamans, avant de me demander : « Ma fille, c'est quoi exactement ton métier dans la qualité ? » Je comprenais parfaitement le sens de sa question. Elle m'observait tout le temps écrire, relire, corriger et publier des articles, des capsules ou des posts sur les réseaux sociaux. Elle me voyait tisser les mots comme on tisse un pagne : avec patience, précision et intention. Pourtant, elle ne cherchait ni à retenir mes acronymes « trop techniques », ni à décoder mes procédures complexes. Elle voulait simplement comprendre ce que je fais, ce que je protège, ce que je construis et, peut-être aussi, ce que j'ai reçu d'elle. Dans notre famille, Maman, le textile n'a jamais été un simple tissu : c'était une manière de vivre, une manière d'aimer. J'ai alors choisi de lui répondre en édifiant un pont entre nos deux mondes : celui du textile et de la rigueur et celui de la recherche et de la pharmacie, portés par le même amour du travail bien fait. Parce que la qualité, Maman, ne se résume pas aux normes et aux certifications. Elle se raconte comme un pagne tissé : fil après fil, geste après geste, vérité après vérité. Après lui avoir ouvert les portes de mon univers, il me fallait lui montrer comment ce métier se construit, jour après jour, point par point. Je lui ai donc expliqué le système qualité à travers le déploiement d'un pagne : un motif harmonieux et organisé, né de gestes simples, mais absolument indispensables. Les 8 fils du système qualité expliqués à Maman Avant d'aborder les procédures ou les documents, il me semblait essentiel de commencer par le geste le plus important dans tous les métiers du fil : écouter avant d'agir. 1. Fil1 _ Comprendre le besoin : écouter avant d'agir (ISO 9001 V2025, §4–5) Maman, tu te souviens quand tu voulais coudre ou acheter une tenue pour quelqu'un ? Tu prenais toujours soin de demander avant : “ Quelle couleur veux-tu ? Quelle coupe ? Pour quelle occasion ?” Tu voulais comprendre avant de créer ou d'acheter. Dans mon métier, c'est exactement pareil. C'est ce qu'on appelle définir l'exigence (ISO 9001 V2025, §4–5) : écouter, comprendre, ne jamais deviner. La qualité commence toujours par cette attention minutieuse. 2. Fil2 _ Organiser : préparer pour que tout se passe bien (ISO 9001 :2015, §6 & §8) « Quand tu préparais un grand repas, tu faisais ta liste, tu vérifiais les ingrédients manquants, tu rangeais ton espace et tu disposais tes ustensiles. Tu planifiais tout pour éviter les surprises. » Dans mon métier, c'est l'étape de la planification, suivie de la réalisation. Chaque procédure, chaque document est un fil que l'on prépare et que l'on place avec intention pour que le motif final reste parfaitement clair. 3. Fil3 _Réaliser : produire avec méthode et vigilance (ISO 9001-V2015, §8) « Quand tu fabriquais ton savon maison, tu respectais rigoureusement les doses, surveillais la cuisson et suivais bien l'ordre des étapes. Tu savais qu'un seul petit écart gâcherait toute la production. En assurance qualité, c'est exactement pareil : nous suivons des procédures strictes et documentons chaque action (la traçabilité). Parce que si un geste échappe, le résultat change, comme un pagne dont un fil glisserait des mains de la tisserande. » 4. Fil4_Vérifier : s'assurer que ce qui a été fait est bon (ISO 9001-V2015, §9) « Une fois ta couture terminée, tu inspectais toujours l'envers et l'endroit. Tu vérifiais l'alignement des points et la propreté des finitions avant de remettre le vêtement. En matière de qualité, on mesure la conformité. Et si un défaut apparaît, on ne le cache pas : on parle de non conformité. C'est comme le fil cassé sur le métier à tisser : on l'arrête, on le répare et on renforce le tissage. » 5. Fil5 _ Corriger : réparer sans déformer le motif (CAPA – ISO 9001-V2015, §10) « Maman, quand une couture lâche, tu ne jettes pas la robe. Tu reprends ton aiguille, tu renforces le fil et tu ajustes la tension. Dans mon métier, c'est pareil ; il s'agit du système CAPA (Actions Correctives et Préventives). Face à un problème, on cherche la cause, on corrige l'incident immédiat et on transforme le processus pour prévenir l'erreur. On ne jette pas le pagne, on le retisse plus fort, plus solide. ». 6. Fil6 _Améliorer : apprendre pour faire mieux demain (PDCA – ISO 9001-V2015,) « À la fin d'une nouvelle recette, maman, tu disais souvent : « La prochaine fois, je mettrai un peu moins de sel ou un peu plus de beurre. » Tu cherchais toujours à améliorer. Dans mon métier, c'est cette quête constante qui prévaut : analyser nos résultats, ajuster nos pratiques et progresser. Chaque retour d'expérience devient un fil plus solide ajouté au pagne. » 7. Fil7 _ Anticiper : penser aux risques avant qu'ils n'arrivent (ISO 9001-V2015, §6.1 ; ISO 31000) « Maman, tu te souviens quand tu faisais sécher tes pagnes dehors ? Tu ne le laissais jamais sur la corde sans surveiller le ciel. Au moindre nuage, tu disais : « On ne laisse pas le pagne à la merci du vent ou de la pluie. » Dans mon métier, c'est ce qu'on appelle la gestion des risques. Anticiper, analyser et prévoir. C'est le fil invisible qui protège la trame bien avant que la tempête n'arrive. 8. Fil 8 _ Piloter : faire vivre le système et garder le cap (ISO 9001, § 5 ; ISO 19011) « Gérer un foyer, c'est veiller chaque jour à l'équilibre entre le bonheur des enfants, la bonne tenue de la maison, les projets et le budget. Tu t'assurais de bonnes prises de décision, tu encourageais et tu réajustais. Piloter un système qualité, c'est similaire : suivre des indicateurs, donner une direction claire et motiver les équipes. La qualité n'est pas un simple bureau ; c'est une culture d'entreprise, une façon de travailler ensemble pour bâtir la confiance. » « Tu vois, Maman ? Le système qualité est comme un grand pagne tissé à huit fils majeurs : écouter, organiser, réaliser, vérifier, corriger, améliorer, anticiper, piloter. Et quand un fil casse, on ne rejette pas le tissu : on le reprend, on le renforce et on le rend plus beau. » Pour lui prouver que cette philosophie n'est pas seulement abstraite, mais qu'elle s'incarne rigoureusement sur le terrain, je lui ai raconté trois anecdotes vécues, au carrefour du textile, de la recherche scientifique et de la pharmacie. Trois histoires pour lui montrer que la qualité vit sur le terrain Anecdote textile : Le Faso Dan Fani qui m'a appris la qualité avant l'heure Je te rappelle une histoire, Maman, que tu avais peut-être oubliée. Quand j'étais enfant, chaque fois que tu achetais un pagne tissé, un vrai Faso Dan Fani, tu le dépliais soigneusement sur la table. Tu lissais chaque pli de la paume de la main en disant : « Un pagne, ma fille, ça ne se choisit pas au hasard. Ça se respecte. » Un jour, je t'ai demandé pourquoi tu accordais autant d'attention à un simple tissu. Tu as souri, de ce sourire qui annonce une grande leçon : « Tu vois cette ligne irrégulière ? La tisserande l'a recommencée trois fois. Le fil cassait. Le motif glissait. Le métier grinçait. Mais elle n'a pas abandonné. Elle a recommencé jusqu'à ce que le geste soit juste. C'est cela, le pagne tissé : la preuve que la qualité n'est pas la perfection… mais la persévérance. » Ce jour-là, j'ai compris que le textile n'était pas seulement un vêtement. C'était une philosophie de vie, un cycle d'amélioration continue transmis de main en main. Chaque fil exprime une exigence, chaque motif est une preuve, chaque irrégularité enseigne une leçon. C'est pour cela que le textile habite toutes mes publications : le pagne tissé est la plus belle métaphore de mon métier. Un travail patient, précis et humble, où chaque détail peut tout changer. » Le pagne m'a enseigné la patience ; la recherche m'a enseigné la rigueur. Ensemble, ils ont façonné ma manière de travailler. Anecdote scientifique : Les 17 minutes qui ont fait vaciller l'étude (CLSI, 2019 ; CLSI, 2020) et l'ICH E6(R3). Ce jour-là, le pagne m'a appris la valeur de chaque fil. Plus tard, la science est venue y ajouter la rigueur de la preuve. Lors d'un essai clinique multicentrique, nous suivions un biomarqueur très prometteur. Les premières analyses étaient excellentes, les tendances stables et les écarts maîtrisés. Tout indiquait un signal scientifique robuste. Cependant, un résultat discordant est apparu : un seul échantillon présentait une valeur totalement aberrante. Cet écart évoquait un élément inattendu dans le processus. Bien que ce résultat ne soit pas alarmant, la qualité refuse l'approximation. Nous avons donc réexaminé l'ensemble des paramètres : les courbes, les centrifugations, les temps de prélèvement, les tubes utilisés, les équipements, les calibrations et les opérateurs. La clé cachée résidait dans un micro-détail inattendu : un délai de 17 minutes entre le prélèvement et la mise en glace du tube. Ce biomarqueur s'est révélé hypersensible à la dégradation pré-analytique. Un simple retard de routine avait suffi à fausser la mesure et, comme j'aime le dire sur ma page Ladyqualityculture, à déformer le motif scientifique. Ni le produit ni le protocole n'étaient en cause, mais un seul geste non maîtrisé dans la chaîne pré-analytique avait suffi à modifier l'ensemble du résultat scientifique, une réalité bien connue des exigences de maîtrise des processus pré-analytiques (CLSI, 2019 ; CLSI, 2020) et des bonnes pratiques cliniques (ICH E6(R3)). En recherche comme sur le métier à tisser : si un fil se rompt, c'est toute la trame qui menace de se défaire. » Anecdote pharmaceutique : Le refus qui a préservé l'intégrité de l'usine (GMP – EMA, 2023 ; WHO GMP, 2020). La recherche m'a montré qu'un détail transforme un résultat ; l'industrie pharmaceutique m'a appris qu'un détail sauve des vies. Dans une unité de production de médicaments, la direction souhaitait accélérer les cadences de production afin de répondre à une urgence critique sur le marché. Face à l'enthousiasme général, l'équipe qualité a pourtant tiré la sonnette d'alarme. Un point précis nous inquiétait : le flux laminaire n'avait jamais été validé pour la nouvelle vitesse de production. Un détail comparable à un fil qui dépasse de l'étoffe. Nous avons posé une seule question, essentielle : « Avez vous validé l'impact de cette vitesse sur la charge particulaire ? » Le silence qui a suivi valait toutes les réponses. C'était non. Augmenter la cadence aurait compromis l'asepsie, exposant ainsi les patients à un risque tangible bien que non immédiatement perceptible. Nous avons opposé un refus ferme, étayé par des arguments et motivé par la volonté de protéger les vies humaines. Ce refus a permis d'interrompre le processus afin de préserver la sécurité. Quelques semaines plus tard, un audit externe confirmait notre décision : la cadence initiale était la seule option sécuritaire. Qu'il s'agisse d'une usine, d'un pagne tissé, d'un essai clinique ou d'une chaîne de production, un seul élément mal maîtrisé peut altérer l'ensemble du résultat (GMP – EMA, 2023 ; WHO GMP, 2020). C'est pourquoi j'utilise la métaphore du textile pour illustrer la notion de qualité : dans le domaine pharmaceutique comme dans l'art du tissage, chaque geste revêt une importance, chaque détail assure la protection, chaque fil révèle une vérité. « Tu vois, Maman ? Ces histoires ne sont pas de simples souvenirs. Elles prouvent que la qualité traverse les domaines comme un fil rouge dans un tissu : elle relie, protège et révèle. C'est ce fil que je voulais te montrer. » Conclusion : Maman, la qualité est une manière d'aimer Maman, tu vois, la qualité dépasse les normes, les audits et les procédures. C'est une manière de travailler et, plus encore, une philosophie de vie. C'est l'art de veiller à ce que chaque action soit juste, sûre, utile et conforme. Cet engagement, je le dois aux patients, aux équipes et aux projets. Mais je te le dois aussi, à toi, qui as toujours veillé à ce que chaque détail de ma vie soit accompli avec soin. En réalité, tu pratiquais déjà la qualité sans la nommer. Tu m'as transmis la rigueur, l'écoute, la précision et l'amour du travail accompli. Mon métier n'est que la suite logique de ton héritage. Et dans chaque projet que je mène, Maman, je cherche encore ce fil que tu m'as donné. En refermant ce récit, une certitude m'habite : la qualité n'est peut-être pas une simple méthodologie. C'est une façon d'aimer, de prendre soin et de donner du sens. Et si, au fond, elle était l'art suprême de tisser la confiance, fil après fil, à l'image de ce que tu as toujours fait pour moi ? Cette philosophie se résume à une pensée qui m'est chère : « Le tissu le plus solide est celui dont chaque fil a été choisi avec intention. » Références Normes internationales 1. ISO. ISO 9001:2015 – Quality management systems — Requirements. Geneva : International Organization for Standardization, 2015. 2. ISO. ISO 9001:2026 – Quality management systems — Requirements (Révision en cours). Geneva : International Organisation for Standardization, 2026. 3. ISO. ISO 14001:2026 – Environmental management systems — Requirements with guidance for use. Geneva : International Organization for Standardization, 2026. 4. ISO. ISO 19011:2026 – Guidelines for auditing management systems. Geneva : International Organization for Standardization, 2026. Bonnes pratiques pharmaceutiques & cliniques 1. ICH. ICH E6(R3) – Good Clinical Practice (Draft). International Council for Harmonization, 2025. 2. European Medicines Agency. EU Guidelines for Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP). EMA, 2023. 3. WHO. WHO Good Manufacturing Practices for Pharmaceutical Products. World Health Organization, 2020. Références scientifiques implicites 1. CLSI. Collection, Transport, and Processing of Blood Specimens for Testing Plasma-Based Coagulation Assays ; Approved Guideline. Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute, 2019. 2. CLSI. Pre-examination Processes in Laboratory Diagnostics. CLSI, 2020. 3. https://parcourscroises.com/comment/view/2173268/2172672 À toi, Maman, qui m'a appris que la qualité naît d'abord de l'amour du travail bien fait. Dr Bougouma Edith Christiane Tisser la confiance, protéger le motif, honorer l'héritage. LadyQualityCulture : la qualité, à la fois art et science. becqualityculture@gail.com

items.title: Opération Togo propre : Les populations des Savanes assainissent leurs cadres de vie
items.description: Dapaong, 2 août (ATOP) – Les populations de la région des Savanes ont assaini leurs cadres de vie, le samedi 1 er aout, conformément à la journée « Togo propre » initiée par le gouvernement. Ces activités ont mobilisé les forces vives des différentes communes autour des autorités locales, dans le but de rendre l’environnement plus sain et agréable à vivre. L’opération à Takpamba A Dapaong, les locaux de la mairie de Tône 1, le marché de Djitague (Tône 2), celui de Lotogou (Tône 3), le marché du carrefour Tantoga et le Centre médicosocial (CMS) de Korbongou dans le Tône 4 ont été entretenus par les populations. A Cinkassé, la population de la commune 1 a mis au propre la cours et les locaux de la Douane de Cinkassé. Dans la commune Oti 1, l’Ecole primaire publique (EPP) Eyadema de Mango a été assaini par la population, tandis qu’à Barkoissi (Oti 2), les citoyens ont rendu propre les locaux de la mairie, le grand marché de la localité, ainsi que les alentours de la poste et de la gendarmerie. La douane de Cinkassé mise au propre A Gando, dans la commune Oti-Sud 1, l’opération Togo propre a permis de nettoyer les locaux de la mairie, les caniveaux et les rues des quartiers Djé-Namoni et Djé-Bouri. A Takpamba, dans l’Oti-Sud 2, ce sont les locaux du nouveau site du commissariat, l’ancien marché de la ville, les alentours de la mairie et le centre communautaire de la localité qui ont été mis au propre. Dans chaque commune, les autorités locales ont remercié leurs administrés pour leur mobilisation. Elles les ont exhortés à toujours garder leurs environnements sains et à se prémunir contre les maladies liées à l’insalubrité. ATOP/JK/DHK/KYA
